evidence: spec/1.5.0.md:113-118 '`critical_path`, the longest chain by count of not-done epics that the gate's members depend on ... and the heaviest such chain by summed estimate when every epic in it has one ... otherwise its estimate is the sum of its bound tasks''; :84-86 (`tp epic done` has no dependency precondition); :165 row 12 'the chain, a done' (the done epic sits at the head, so a mid-chain done epic is never exercised).
finding: `critical_path` can be computed two ways, and both readings fit the sentence. (1) 'The longest chain by count of not-done epics' reads either as a path weighted by how many of its epics are not done, so a done epic in the middle is skipped and the path continues, or as a chain made only of not-done epics, so a done epic cuts it. A done epic in the middle of a not-done chain is reachable: `tp epic done` has no dependency precondition (§5), and dependencies fall back (§3/§4). On a→b→c→d with only b done, one implementation reports [a, c, d] and the other reports [c, d]. (2) 'The heaviest such chain by summed estimate when every epic in it has one' reads either as 'heaviest among the chains whose epics all have estimates' or as 'reported only when every candidate chain is fully estimated'. Separately, an epic whose estimate is 'the sum of its bound tasks'' while only some of those tasks carry `estimate_minutes` may or may not 'have one'. §10 row 12 ('the chain, a done') tests neither case.

For any epic with bound tasks the estimate is already derivable ('otherwise its estimate is the sum of its bound tasks''), so the field only weights not-yet-specced epics in a view-only chain. It adds a schema key, a `tp epic set` write path, carry-over obligations for whole-object writers (§8) and an export field without feeding any decision an agent makes (ready, claim, gate, block).

finding: `tp epic claim <id> [--by <name>]` adds a flag and a stored `claimed.by` key that no rule reads: a second claim is refused on the claim's existence alone, `--release` removes any claim regardless of holder, `claimed` status (§3) ignores the holder, and `tp epic ready` excludes any claim. The task-level `tp claim` has no `--by`, so this is a new surface an agent must decide to fill with nothing depending on the answer.
